item.title: SIGNED | Wrexham AFC sign Bailey Cadamarteri from Sheffield Wednesday
item.description: Wrexham AFC are delighted to confirm the signing of Bailey Cadamarteri from fellow Championship side Sheffield Wednesday for an undisclosed fee. The 20-year-old striker has signed a contract until the end of the 2028/29 season. After progressing through their academy to sign professionally in 2022, Cadamarteri made 30 appearances for The Owls this season, netting two goals in the process – including one against Wrexham when the two sides met at the STōK Cae Ras in August. item.title: CLUB NEWS | Sam Smith nominated for PFA Fans' January POTM
item.description: Wrexham AFC forward Sam Smith has been nominated for January’s PFA Championship Fans’ Player of the Month Award. Smith enjoyed a fantastic month for the Red Dragons, scoring four league goals and playing a key role as Phil Parkinson’s side climbed into the play-off positions. In total, Wrexham picked up 13 points in six matches, with the 27-year-old scoring against Blackburn Rovers, Derby County, Norwich City and Sheffield Wednesday. item.description: Our Sky Bet Championship fixture away to Watford at Vicarage Road, on Saturday March 7, will now kick off at 12.30pm having been selected for live TV coverage on Sky Sports+. item.title: CONTRACT NEWS | Reuben Egan signs contract until end of 2025/26 season
item.description: Wrexham AFC are delighted to confirm that goalkeeper Reuben Egan has signed a contract extension until the end of the 2025/26 season. The Irish shot-stopper joined Wrexham on a six-month contract in September 2025, following a successful trial with the Club. Egan spent a season with Tranmere Rovers before initially joining Wrexham and will continue to bolster the goalkeeping department for the remainder of this campaign.

item.title: SQUAD LIST | Wrexham AFC make updated 2025/26 submission
item.description: In line with EFL regulations, Wrexham AFC has submitted the following list of players aged 21 and older for its updated 2025/26 squad list. EFL regulations provide that all EFL Championship clubs can name 25 players aged 21 and older in the squad. This includes both goalkeepers and outfield players. We have opted to initially name 23 players at this stage, providing us with the option to add two extra players as needed.
